title: Maintain alternating chat history for empty or thought-only model responses
body:
### What happened?

The issue is a flaw in the `recordHistory` method's logic. When the model's response contained only non-visible content (like a `thought` part), the method would filter it out but then fail to add a placeholder empty `model` turn. This would either leave two consecutive `user` turns in the history (in streaming mode) or simply an incomplete turn, causing tests to fail and breaking conversational integrity.

### What did you expect to happen?

The user and model turns should alternate.

linked_prs.title: Ensure a Strictly Alternating Message History
linked_prs.body:
## TLDR

This pull request fixes a critical bug in `GeminiChat` where the chat history would become invalid if the model returned a response that only contained "thought" parts or was completely empty. This led to incorrect history length and failed conversations.

The fix ensures that an empty `model` turn is always added to the history in these scenarios, preserving the required alternating `user`/`model` structure. The tests have also been corrected to properly validate this behavior.

## Dive Deeper

The root cause of the issue was a flaw in the `recordHistory` method's logic. When the model's response contained only non-visible content (like a `thought` part), the method would filter it out but then fail to add a placeholder empty `model` turn. This would either leave two consecutive `user` turns in the history (in streaming mode) or simply an incomplete turn, causing tests to fail and breaking conversational integrity.

This PR replaces the old, complex logic with a single, robust `recordHistory` method. This new implementation correctly performs **intra-part consolidation**—merging adjacent text parts within a single response—while correctly handling all edge cases we discovered (thoughts, mixed content types, and malformed data).

During this process, we discovered that several existing unit tests for consolidation were flawed, as they were written to expect the buggy data-loss behavior. These tests have been corrected to assert the proper, intended behavior, which locks in the fix and prevents future regressions.
